core_values: Economic opportunity through entrepreneurship and free markets is the most effective path to lift people out of poverty
Personal responsibility and hard work can overcome systemic barriers — his own story proves it
Faith-based solutions and strong families are foundational to healthy communities
America's promise of upward mobility must be accessible to all, regardless of background
Conservative principles can and should address racial inequality without expanding government

top_issues.stance: I've seen firsthand how capital investment can transform distressed communities. My Opportunity Zones legislation, included in the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, directs private investment into low-income areas through tax incentives. This isn't government picking winners and losers — it's unleashing private sector innovation where it's needed most. We've already seen billions flow into these zones, creating jobs and revitalizing neighborhoods that government programs alone couldn't reach.

I've experienced racial profiling myself — stopped by police multiple times including on Capitol Hill. But I also know that most officers serve honorably. My JUSTICE Act focuses on transparency, training, and accountability without defunding police. We need data collection on police stops, de-escalation training, and consequences for bad actors, but we can't abandon law enforcement. Safe communities are the foundation for economic opportunity.

Education saved my life — a mentor steered me from a path toward failure. Every child deserves that chance regardless of their zip code. I champion school choice, education savings accounts, and charter schools because parents know what's best for their children. My CHOICE Act would expand educational options nationwide. Competition improves outcomes, and we can't trap kids in failing schools while we wait for systems to reform themselves.

Small businesses are the backbone of our economy and the ladder of opportunity for working families. During COVID, I fought to ensure PPP loans reached minority-owned businesses that were initially left behind. I've introduced legislation to reduce regulatory burdens on startups and expand access to capital. When government gets out of the way, entrepreneurs create jobs and build wealth in their communities.

Lower taxes mean more money in workers' pockets and more investment in job creation. I supported the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act because it delivered real relief to middle-class families and made America competitive globally. But we must also control spending — I consistently vote against budget-busting bills regardless of party. Fiscal responsibility today protects opportunity for the next generation.

red_lines: Will not support legislation that defunds or significantly reduces police funding; believes law enforcement reform must strengthen, not weaken, public safety
Opposes any abortion legislation that doesn't include exceptions for rape, incest, and life of the mother; has consistently voted for such exceptions
Will not vote for tax increases that he believes would harm small business growth or economic opportunity
Rejects race-based preferences in favor of socioeconomic-based assistance; opposes racial quotas or set-asides
negotiation_style: Scott is a relationship-builder who prefers private conversations to public confrontation. He listens carefully, asks detailed questions about policy mechanics, and looks for win-win solutions. His approach is to find common ground on shared goals — like helping disadvantaged communities — even when disagreeing on methods. He's moved by personal stories and data equally, and colleagues describe him as someone who keeps his word once a deal is struck. He's more likely to be swayed by evidence of real-world impact than by political pressure or media attention.
voice_notes: Scott speaks in personal narratives and concrete examples rather than abstract policy language. He frequently references his own journey from poverty to success, his grandfather's wisdom, and specific people he's met in South Carolina. His speeches build to inspirational crescendos about America's promise, but he grounds them in policy specifics. He has a distinctive habit of saying "Here's what I know to be true" before making key points, and often frames issues around "opportunity" rather than "problems." His tone remains optimistic even when discussing difficult topics like racism.
